canonical_source.title: Linguistic Survey of India: West Bengal, Part I (Mundari section)
canonical_source.institution: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India

supported_metadata: Mundari is treated as a Non-Scheduled language of India in this survey.
The study reports field data collection in Jhargram of Midnapore district, West Bengal, during August 1995.
The printed text names informants Hari and Phagua Mundari.
The study states that its Mundari data are based on Midnapore district, West Bengal.
The survey keeps Census language/mother-tongue classification explicit rather than silently merging Munda and Mundari categories.

identity_and_dependency_controls.canonicalization_rule: Treat catalogue pages, search snippets, mirrors, downloads and citations of this LSI section as manifestations/references to one government survey source unless independent underlying evidence is demonstrated.
identity_and_dependency_controls.upstream_dependency_note: Historical statements explicitly attributed by the section to Grierson/LSI Vol. IV or Census publications remain dependencies and are not independent corroboration by this source.
identity_and_dependency_controls.fieldwork_dependency_note: The 1995 elicitation event is underlying fieldwork represented by the publication; publication and fieldwork are not two independent corroborating sources.

rights_consent_cultural_access.rule: Government publication/public access does not establish permission to redistribute underlying elicitation data, participant consent, community validation, or unrestricted cultural access.
